Total number of questions — 20
165
Development of logistic parks
*521. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Railways plan to develop
logistic parks to serve as 'one-stop shop' at
various places alongside the route of the
proposed dedicated freight corridor;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what are the details of plots that are
proposed to be developed on the ECoR
system?
Laying of water pipelines crossing the
railway track
*522. SHRI JAYANTILAL BAROT:
SHRI  SURENDRA MOTILAL
PATEL:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is necessary for the States
to get permission from the railway
authorities for laying water pipelines where
these have to cross the railway track;
(b) if so, whether the delay in permission
caused the delay in implementation of the
projects;
(c) the number of such proposals
received from the various States which are
pending with the Railways for the last three
years, particularly for the State of Gujarat;
and
(d) by when these proposals would be
cleared?
Reduction of maternal deaths
*523. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that out of one
lakh deliveries, 300 pregnant women die
every year and with only an average of 16
point reduction in figure, India cannot reach
its Millennium Development Goals of
lowering the maternal deaths to 200 by
2007 and 109 by 2015;
(b) whether this conclusion is based on
the study report released by Government
in October, 2006;

166
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) whether after receiving the report,
strong Government policies would be
required to meet the target; and
(d) if so, the steps Government propose
to achieve the target set up by 2015?
Dependence on edible oil import
†*524. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the attention of
Government has been drawn towards the
White Paper related to oilseed sector
released by the Solvent Extract on
Association of India;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that the
increasing dependence of the country on
import for supply of edible oils can cause
further crisis; and
(c) if so, the reaction of Government
thereon?
Telephone booths on stations
*525. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that telephone
booths were allotted to handicapped
persons in Railway Stations across the
country under a Central Government
Scheme to rehabilitate the disabled in 1981,
the International Year of Disabled;
(b) if so, how many such booths were
allotted all over the country, Railway Zone-
wise and what are the terms and conditions
of such allotment;
(c) whether it is also a fact that their
agreement has expired on April 27, this year;
(d) if so, whether Government have a
proposal to further extension of the
agreement to the existing booth owners;
and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Modernisation of ECoR
*526. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to spend
around Rs. 3 lakh crore for modernisation
of Railways;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of modernisation projects
that would be undertaken on the ECoR
under this plan head ?
SGC offices
*527. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the Save Grain
Campaign (SGC) offices in the country;
(b) whether it is a fact that there is no
SGC office in Andhra Pradesh;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor;
(d) the details of technologies and
technical know-how developed by the
Indian Grain Storage Management and
Research Institute for benefitting farmers
in minimizing post-harvesting losses in
foodgrains; and
(e) the number of farmers trained under
the SGC in Andhra Pradesh during the last
three years year-wise?

167
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Study on impact of global warming

Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT

towns and cities along India’s eastern coast
would be devastated with global warming
intensifying cyclones and rising sea levels
eroding vast stretches of the shoreline;
(b) if so, whether Government have done
any comprehensive study on the impact of
global warming in the coastal areas;

Setting up of atomic energy plants for
tribal areas
†3812. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to
overtaping of hydel power and uncertain
and expensive availability of coal for
thermal energy, the only option available
in Rajasthan is atomic energy; and
(b) whether Government would make
arrangements for setting up four units of
one thousand megawatt each, so that energy
demand of tribal areas of Rajasthan,
Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat could be met by
the year 2012?
Indo-US agreement on atomic energy
†3813. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
 DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that an agreement
on atomic energy was signed between the
Prime Minister of India and President of
America in the past years, involving the
two countries;
(b) if so, whether in order to execute
this agreement, any talks between the two
countries have been held so far at various
levels;
(c) if so, the number of times such talks
have been held; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

886
(d) the decisions taken so far during such
talks?
Atomic energy generation projects in
India
†3814. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
seven atomic energy generation projects in
India with a generation capacity of 3380
megawatts;
(b) if not, the facts thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that there are
five such projects in Russia and China but
with over 4000 MWe capacity;
(d) if so, whether it is also a fact that
the technique adopted in the field of atomic
energy in India is expected to be more
costlier in comparison to above countries;
and
(e) if so, the facts thereof and the reasons
behind not setting up projects in India on
the lines of those in Russia and China?
Indo-US nuclear agreement
†3815. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
several countries in the world who have
expressed their dissent to the nuclear
agreement signed by India and America on
the 18th July, 2005 for civil purposes;
(b) if so, the names of those countries
and their reactions thereto separately;
(c) whether efforts have been made by
Government to put India's viewpoint before
those countries; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Development of a mega reactor by
NPCIL
3816. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether State-run Nuclear Power
Corporation of India Ltd. (NPCIL) has
launched preparatory work for the
development of a 10,000 mega watt nuclear
power project, with six units of 1,650 mega
watt each in Maharashtra;
(b) whether this is for the first time that
NPCIL is planning such a mega reactor,
and would join France, Germany and
Finland where European pressurized
reactors are being used to develop nuclear
power projects with such high capacities;
and
(c) if so, by when these projects are
likely to be completed?
Improvement of nuclear power
capacity
3817. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the current nuclear power
capacity in India is 3,900 MW which is
about three per cent of the total installed
capacity in India, whereas the percentage
of electricity generated through nuclear
power in the US, Japan and Germany is 19
per cent, 29 per cent and 31 per cent,
respectively;
(b) whether Government are hopeful
that the existing nuclear power capacity
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

887
would increase to 7,280 MW by the end of
the Eleventh Five Year Plan period; and
(c) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to improve the nuclear power
capacity further?
Coal royalty rates

SINGHVI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:

rates are likely to go up and the States
producing coal and Lignite would get a
substantial rise;
(b) if so, the estimated benefit which
each coal and Lignite producing State would
get; and
(c) whether such States would be
advised to spend a major portion of the
enhanced royalty amount towards latest
state-of-the-art safety measures as the
